# Steel stocks: how to analyze steel companies

**Steel stocks are shares in companies turning ore and scrap into construction's base material — and few sectors swing harder between profit and loss: same mill, same furnaces — the result depends on where in the cycle volume and price stand.** The [steel sector course](/kurser/se-23-stalsektorn) calls the furnace the market's purest cycle machine; AK1A's universe carries the sector on four names, four exchanges, four countries — SSAB, Nucor, ArcelorMittal, Nippon Steel — two raw material routes, two value triangles, one shared cycle.

## The steel cycle — three legs carry demand

Demand rests on three legs: construction (homes, offices, structural steel), infrastructure (bridges, rail, power grids), capital goods (machines, vehicles, tools). No leg owns the cycle alone; together they create the lag: housing credit hits structural steel with delay — [housing market mechanics](/kurser/ma-08-bostadsmarknadens-mekanik) owns the transmission — capital goods have their own [business cycle indicators](/kurser/ma-04-konjunkturindikatorerna). Geography: in the middle of the 2010s roughly half the world's steel was cast in one country, China; when its construction broke the surplus went global — price falls, closures, [cycle risk](/kurser/rk-05-cykelrisk) in pure form. Europe idled tonnage first, furnaces after. First rule: demand is a weighted basket; the turn arrives at different times in the legs. Weight by customer structure: structural steel in housing credit, vehicle and machinery steel in the order book, grid steel its own slower wave.

## Raw material leverage — ore, scrap, coal and power

Two chemical routes lead to one ton — the arithmetic starts in the cost basket. The integrated mill: variable cost 1,900 kronor per ton — 1,100 iron ore, 350 coking coal, 200 process energy, 250 labor and other. The scrap arc mill: same total, different map — 1,200 scrap, 400 electricity, 100 electrodes and other, 200 labor. Sensitivity is multiplication: ore up 30 percent costs the ore mill 1,100 × 0.30 = 330 kronor per ton — the scrap mill notices nothing; power up 50 percent costs the scrap mill 400 × 0.50 = 200 — the ore mill barely moves. Ore is priced globally by mine supply — the [mining and metals sector's](/kurser/se-20-gruv-och-metallsektorn) world; steel rolled here. Scrap is steel's own mirror — steel falls, scrap follows — the raw material fall neutralizes part of the price fall — hence the scrap mill's calmer swing; the ore mill lacks the brake. The contract share sets the speed into the income statement: quarterly prices shadow spot a quarter behind — reports mirror last quarter. The large clock is the [commodity cycle guide](/blogg/ravarubolag-materialbranschens-cykel); this is the furnace's arithmetic.

## Blast furnace versus scrap arc — the ladder in the cost curve

The routes carry two capital structures. The blast furnace mill is heavy — the course's example: fixed costs 4,000 million kronor per year; the next capacity step 12 billion for one million tons per year — 12,000 kronor per annual ton, a forty-year decision. The scrap mill is light: 700 million fixed, the furnace pausable for weeks when prices say so. At a volume fall to 60 percent of capacity the scrap mill shows 0.48 million tons × 1,500 kronor = 720 million, minus the fixed 700 — near zero — the blast furnace mill on the same fall minus 400 million. Same cycle, different consequence: [cost position](/kurser/mt-06-kostnadsoverlagsenhet) is read in the cost basket, not the catalog. Nucor, the scrap school's flagship: gross margin 30.3 percent in 2021, 12.0 in 2025 — yet 53 straight dividend increases, capex through the bottom: 1,622 to 3,422 million dollars. Building when cheap is the scrap signature — see [dividend basics](/blogg/utdelningar-101) for the chain. The balance sheet completes it: interest coverage 28.74, beta 1.88 — the cycle in beta form — carry the bottom years; lower fixed cost per ton, smaller cushion.

## Steel stocks' operating leverage — when the margin swings

The course's example shows furnace leverage in three steps. Contract price 3,400 kronor per ton, variable cost 1,900: contribution 3,400 − 1,900 = 1,500. At full capacity, 4.0 million tons: 6,000 million contribution minus 4,000 fixed — plus 2,000 million. At 60 percent utilization (2.4 million tons): contribution 3,600, result minus 400. Fixed cost per ton rises from 1,000 at full utilization to 1,667 at 60 percent. Every tenth of a utilization unit: 600 million in result. Price amplifies too: spot down 20 percent with 70 percent contracts blends the price to 3,196 — minus 6.0 percent — the contribution to 1,296 — minus 13.6 percent: leverage 2.3 times; the variable cost does not follow the price down. Reality carries the pattern: SSAB swung from minus 10,886 million kronor in 2022 to plus 13,029 million in 2023 — 23,915 million in one year; revenue fell 7.2 percent. Nucor's result fell from 7,576 million dollars in 2022 to 1,737 million in 2025, minus 77.1 percent. [The margin ladder and operating leverage](/kurser/ln-03-marginaltrappan-och-operativ-havstavng) own the mechanics — the steel calculation their purest example; the trough year's [solvency and interest coverage](/kurser/st-01-soliditet-och-rantetackning) the sector's other side.

## Supply inertia — the blast furnace as a 40-year decision

Demand curves swing in years; supply in decades. The blast furnace is a 40-year decision, three to four years of construction: in good years every mill sees the same calculation, expands — five mills each adding 20 percent grow supply by a fifth, no single board deciding it — tonnage arrives next phase, often against turned demand. Consolidation answers: Nippon Steel's fiscal 2026 became the consolidation year — result 17.2 billion yen from 637.3, goodwill from 71.6 to 259.7 billion — a balance sheet buying tonnage instead of building it. The [World Steel Association](https://www.worldsteel.org/) follows production country by country — the supply position's reference surface. The mirror holds upward: idled capacity takes years to wake; price outbreaks come when demand turns against supply closed early. Decarbonization writes the next chapter: hydrogen instead of coke as reduction agent — the Swedish HYBRIT line — moves the cost mass from coal to power; electricity becomes the new raw material question, at the pace the power system allows.

## Steel stocks' valuation — the multiple follows the cycle

Valuation follows the cycle, not its average. In the universe ArcelorMittal trades at a P/B of exactly 1.00, Nippon Steel at 0.59 — 695 yen against a book value of 1,078 — Nucor, with scrap-mill capital discipline, at 2.72, SSAB at 1.46. The P/E carries the cycle trap: ArcelorMittal at 31.31 on a trough year when the result was 6.1 percent of the peak year's — expensive multiple, small profit — the peak year's low multiple looks cheap just as the next downturn waits. SSAB at 18.5 after falling earnings: the same warning. Therefore [normalized multiples](/kurser/vr-02-normaliserade-multipler) are the standard tool: the earnings base belongs to the cycle's average, not the latest quarter's ton price — read the [P/B course](/kurser/v05-pb) for balance sheet testimony, [the P/E ratio's warnings](/kurser/km-009-pe) for the trap, compare against the [sector medians](/blogg/branschmedianer-akm2). The [sector analysis method](/kurser/se-16-sektoranalysens-metod) gathers the questions. The rule is nearly mechanical: at trough volume P/E looks expensive, P/B cheap, at peak the reverse — book capital does not cycle, earnings do.

## Checklist: seven questions when you analyze steel stocks

1. **The cycle leg** — homes, infrastructure, capital goods: which weighted basket carries the volume, how late does the rate hit tonnage?
2. **The cost basket** — ore or scrap: what does a 30 percent ore shock, a 50 percent power shock, cost per ton in this mill?
3. **The capital structure** — fixed costs per ton at full and half utilization: where is the zero line, how deep the trough?
4. **The processing level** — strip steel at 3,400 kronor per ton or qualified core plate at 12,000, where switching supplier takes a year of testing — the [switching cost](/kurser/mt-05-byteskostnader-och-inlasning) moat protects the ladder.
5. **The survival measure** — how many trough years can the balance sheet take before dividend and solvency feel it? Count the trough first, the multiple last.
6. **The supply position** — what do competitors build now, how much capacity was idled in the last trough? Does demand face supply already closed?
7. **The cycle position in the multiple** — is the P/E read on peak or trough earnings? Normalize before comparing.

Steel stocks reward those who ask which raw material route and cycle position a report belongs to — then reckon the furnace's leverage by hand before the multiple. The whole is in the [complete guide to Swedish stock analysis](/blogg/komplett-guide-svensk-aktieanalys-2026). The worked examples are pedagogical constructions; the four real names carry the same mechanics in their reports.
